title: Effect of Tempering Temperature on Microstructure and Mechanical Properties of Cr–Ni–Mo–V Rotor Steel
content: The influence of tempering temperature on the microstructure and mechanical properties of Cr–Ni–Mo–V rotor steel for large rotors was investigated. The microstructure was characterized by scanning electron microscope, transmission electron microscope and X-ray diffraction, and the mechanical properties were tested by uniaxial tensile test. The results show that as the tempering temperature increases from 450 ℃ to 700 ℃, the strength of Cr–Ni–Mo–V rotor steel first decreases, then increases and then decreases again, and the plasticity gradually increases. The main reason is that with the increase of tempering temperature, the gradual recovery and recrystallization of lat martensite lead to a decrease in dislocation density in the matrix, and the carbide gradually changes from a large number of rod-shaped continuous Fe3Mo3C distribution to a spherical Mo2C and VC distribution, resulting in Fe3Mo3C precipitation and resolution, and dispersion precipitation of Mo2C and VC. Therefore, the change in strength is mainly influenced by the balance between the strengthening of the solid solution, the strengthening of the precipitation and the strengthening of the dislocation in the matrix.
